tagline: Up the Mad River under the limestone cliffs.
intro: Out of Medway, Lower Valley Pike runs about 11 miles up the Mad River toward Springfield as County Road 316, between limestone cliffs and riparian woods, with wetlands alongside. Christopher Gist, one of the first English explorers here, came upon the river in flood and called it the Mad River, and the name is for its broken, rapid current.
It is the largest coldwater fishery in Ohio, and the state stocks it from time to time with rainbow and brown trout.

moments.title: Peckuwe
moments.text: At the Shawnee town of Piqua, Clark's militia shelled the stockade from the river cliffs, and rather than rebuild, the Shawnee moved to the Great Miami River and took the name with them.

moments.title: Huffman House
moments.text: Jacob Huffman, one of Clark County's earliest settlers, spent seven years from 1825 quarrying local limestone and cutting it with refined detail for this house, which has a family cemetery beside it.

moments.title: Mad River Gorge
moments.text: Cliffs of 45 to 50 feet rise in this gorge park on the Mad River, and anyone may climb them, at no cost and at their own risk.
